title: Small services with clear jobs
summary: A service is a part that does work for another part. Microservices divide an app by jobs, such as catalog search and lending.
introduction: A service is a part that does work for another part. Microservices divide an app by jobs, such as catalog search and lending. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain small services with clear jobs
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A service is a part that does work for another part. Microservices divide an app by jobs, such as catalog search and lending.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: This is a design course using worked examples. It does not add services to this website. A small project is often easier as one application.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Microservices. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Catalog service: book titles and authors
Loan service: who borrowed each copy
Browser: shows results to a learner
blocks.title: Small services with clear jobs

blocks.text: The jobs are separated by purpose. Merely splitting files does not create useful service boundaries.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Choose two jobs in a school canteen system.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Many tiny services can be harder to manage than one clear application.
For more detail later, use this [Microservices further reading](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/microservices/).
